extracted.intended_audience: Snopes readers, tip submitters, potential contributors, and members
extracted.subtask_description: FAQ and editorial-policy guidance describing how Snopes selects, researches, rates, corrects, and publishes fact checks and other content, plus site policies on ads, membership, reproduction, and user submissions. Intended to explain standards and procedures readers and tipsters should expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of satire
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter how unbelievable a story may seem to you, another person is taking it at face value — as a factual recounting of real-life events. Whether you agree with something being described as 'satire' or 'parody' is a matter of opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snopes will cover material described as satire because some people treat it as factual; classification as satire/parody can be subjective, so coverage is driven by whether the item is being treated as a factual claim by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest posts policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Snopes does not accept, nor review, articles submitted by others for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want something fact-checked or investigated by Snopes, use the contact form rather than submitting an article for direct publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling political pieces — attribution vs factual analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: When a political piece is primarily an editorial or other expression of opinion, we tag it as such and attempt to verify only whether the attribution is correct. When a political piece purports to offer facts, we place it in a relevant category and analyze the factual claims made within for veracity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinions are not falsifiable, so Snopes focuses on objective elements (e.g., who wrote it) for opinion pieces, and on factual claims when the piece presents verifiable assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy is to promptly correct errors of fact and to clarify any potentially confusing or ambiguous statements in our articles and fact checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever Snopes changes the rating of a fact check, corrects or modifies a substantive supporting fact (even if it doesn't affect the overall rating), or adds substantial new information, those changes are noted and explained in an Update box at the foot of the article. Typographical errors and minor non-substantive revisions are not noted. Text inside colored boxes (collected folklore/quotations) is reproduced exactly and not edited for orthography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting items for fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers are welcome to send links to articles, social media posts, or images using the contact form; include screenshots or attachments with as much information as possible, including when and where you found the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to volume, Snopes may not respond personally. Use short keywords to search the site first (overly long/specific searches yield fewer results). Attach supporting materials where possible to help evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-selection criteria (what tips Snopes looks for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes cannot fact-check every dubious claim; they try to tackle what seems most prominent each day: items top of mind for readers, viral rumors that could lead to misunderstandings, and purported trivia facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs used to identify topics include site search term tabulations, reader email submissions, comments and social media posts, external social media, and what's trending on Google and social platforms. Resource constraints limit coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry is assigned to a member of the editorial staff who undertakes preliminary research and writes the first draft. Research generally begins with attempting to contact the source of the claim and individuals/organizations with expertise, and searching published information (news, scientific/medical journals, books, transcripts, statistics, archives, public records, and reputable videos/photos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snopes attempts to use non-partisan information and data sources (e.g., peer-reviewed journals, government statistics) as much as possible and alerts readers when sources are partisan. Other staff may contribute research or expertise; the final product passes through at least one editor and is revised further if not meeting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Snopes decides what to write about
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes fact-checks items readers ask about or search for, as well as viral rumors that could lead to misunderstandings and purported trivia facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage decisions are not made based on political orientation; the volume of available resources and staffing constrains coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating-system guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Distilling the veracity of a topic or event into a one-word assessment can be challenging. Our rating system has a variety of labels so we can be accurate, clear and fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's important to note the claim statement on each article because the specific wording of the claim is what the rating evaluates — the rating applies to the claim statement, not broader impressions or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban-legend ('Legend') classification
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'urban legend' is a tale that circulates widely, is told and retold with differing details (or exists in multiple versions), and is said to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the events described ever actually occurred is irrelevant to classification as an urban legend; the classification is based on transmission, variability, and being presented as true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication without 'True'/'False' rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Snopes content (original news stories, in-depth investigations, and other material to help readers understand and contextualize information) is published without a True/False rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact checks that use the rating system are clearly labeled; other content serves different informational purposes and may not receive a simple veracity label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of sources (showing work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research materials used in the preparation of any fact check are listed so that readers who wish to verify the validity of our information may check those sources for themselves. Click the 'Sources' button at the bottom of an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snopes emphasizes showing work so readers can independently verify claims; readers are encouraged to keep looking for information if skeptical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and linking policy (copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Using our material without our permission is copyright infringement, even if your site is noncommercial, and even if you give us credit. You are welcome to link to any of our articles from your site, but you may not reproduce the content of our pages on your own site or distribute text via email or message boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprinting interferes with Snopes' ability to update material and deprives them of advertising revenue necessary to operate the site; permission is required for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: API and data access policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes does not have an API available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations interested in access to fact-check data should contact Snopes to discuss potential commercial opportunities; researchers/academic institutions may contact Snopes to discuss reduced barriers to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and engagement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes does not host on-site comment sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid the costs and moderation burden of comment hosting, Snopes prefers readers to discuss on social media or in the Facebook group; readers can also send questions, corrections, or concerns via the contact form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising funding and adblock troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes is funded by ad revenue and subscriptions; readers are asked to allow ads or join paid membership to cover editorial costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adblocker prompts appear, users should check for built-in browser blockers, privacy/tracking extensions, private browsing mode, or try another browser. After adding exceptions, users may need to restart their browser. If problems persist, contact Snopes with browser version and troubleshooting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ad content quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes filters out ads that advocate partisan political causes or candidates, flash excessively, contain adult material, play (non-user-initiated) audio, spawn multiple windows, automatically trigger downloads, install malware, or misleadingly claim visitors have won contests or report viruses/spyware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite aggressive quality controls, some malicious or misleading ads may get through due to the scale and geo-targeting of ad exchanges; Snopes monitors and blocks bad actors when identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ad complaint and remediation process
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter an ad issue on Snopes, contact adops@snopes.com with details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as many details as possible (advertiser name, description, or a screenshot). Geo-targeting can make it difficult for Snopes to see problematic ads themselves without screenshots and detailed reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cookies and security-software notifications explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most internet advertising exchanges use cookies to keep track of which ads have been displayed to a visitor; these cookies do not acquire personal information and are used for targeting and measuring ad effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some security programs may flag such cookies as 'adware' or mistakenly report cookie placement as attempts to download software. Users uncomfortable with cookies can delete them or change browser settings to prevent acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passwordless login rationale and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes uses a passwordless login system because it is more secure, simpler, and becoming the norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Password reuse and weak passwords create risk; with passwordless login, accounts are tied to email and require keeping the login page open while checking email for the temporary code. Desktop users should use two tabs; mobile users may need to open a separate browser to retrieve codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership benefits and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Memberships allow readers to support Snopes and offer benefits like ad-free browsing, a community badge, and a members-only Snopes Digest newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memberships are added to a free Snopes account; direct contributions are separate from memberships. Memberships are purchased via the membership page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership login/session rules and troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: Members don't need to log in every time, but must log in again after 3 consecutive days (72 hours) of inactivity. After purchasing membership you receive email to register for a Snopes Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can't get the verification code while keeping the login page open, use tabbed browsing on desktop or open a separate browser on mobile. If verification emails don't arrive, check spam/junk/promotions and contact accounts@snopes.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership cancellation and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You can cancel your membership at any time. Past membership payments are final and non-refundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly recurring memberships can be cancelled from the account page. One-time contributions and individual membership payments are final and non-refundable. For other purchases consult the full return policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting site technical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Report site errors via the contact form or by emailing community@snopes.com with a brief description and screenshots if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screenshots and as much detail as possible to help troubleshoot the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal data handling and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes processes personal data as stated in the Privacy Policy and uses email and targeted advertising for product/service updates and marketing communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users may withdraw consent or manage preferences at any time (unsubscribe links or contact). Snopes will not share your email without permission.
